title: Individual-investor landlords: segment lead, no customer problem yet evidenced

history.reason: Segment-size signal from HUD/Census; no pain point established.
Review correction: removed settled ownership/property-count claims because the HUD release mixes unit/property denominators; retained only clearly labeled housing-unit scope.

provenance.session: session_01LQxkVvFKqYivoTtCXoQ4cs; reviewed corrections by Codex fix_merge_30_31

description: HUD reports that nearly 46% of US rental units are in 1–4 unit properties. Individual-investor landlords are a segment to investigate, but the release’s ownership counts mix units and properties; no owner-population size or specific unmet administrative problem is established here.
customer_segment: Individual-investor owners of 1-4 unit rental properties.
context: Scoping lead only: identifies a housing/property type for further investigation, not quantified individual-owner population or a customer problem. Do not treat as validated demand.

evidence.text: The HUD release reports 49.5 million US rental housing units, nearly 46% of them in properties with 1–4 units. These are housing-unit figures, not counts of landlords or small businesses.

alternatives: Property-management software and services: not investigated.

contradictory_evidence.text: Segment size alone does not show an unmet problem or willingness to pay.

uncertainty: Unknown: management practices, rent collection and screening pain, tool adoption, and spend. This record exists to avoid re-scoping the segment. The ownership percentage/count denominator in the HUD summary is unresolved; verify RHFS tables before quantifying individual-investor owners or mortgaged small properties.
open_questions: How do small landlords currently collect rent, screen tenants and keep records?
Which tasks cause the most time or loss?
next_actions: Read Census RHFS tables on management and operating expenses, then seek primary evidence of specific pain points.
